notes: Canonical requirement catalogue. `claims` link to evidence/claims_register.json. Design, code, test and eval links are discovered by scripts/traceability.mjs, which scans the repository for each REQ ID. scope: MVP = Phase 2 build; LATER = after the pilot (Gate 4) or needs a backend.

requirements.text: The activity library groups activities by goal: joint attention and turn-taking, anticipation and requesting, early words, following instructions, motor skills, emotional regulation, transitions, and sibling or peer play.
Each activity shows step-by-step guidance, at least one 'pause and wait' prompt, and tips, all loaded from the governed content store.
Each activity has a model audio example the caregiver can play with a tap. Nothing plays automatically.
Each activity displays its evidence tier and source section, with a link to the matching Education Hub entry.
A guided session lasts 10–15 minutes and is made up of 2–4 activities.
The session player shows caregiver cue cards (for example 'pause 5–10 s', 'copy your child') at each step.
At the end of a session the caregiver records participation (did we play together; which activities; how engaged) in 30 seconds or less. No performance scores.
Each routine (tidy-up, bath, teeth, leaving the house, bedtime, mealtime) has one fixed short song that stays the same every time.
Routine songs link to a visual schedule of picture steps.
Caregivers can record their own voice for a routine song. Recordings stay on the device and play through the Child Mode audio safety chain.
The child chooses the tracks on their calm playlist using picture cards.
Calm tracks are slow and quiet. An optional sway or breathing visual moves slowly, and is still when reduced motion is on.
The child controls the volume in the Regulation Corner, always within the Child Mode ceiling.
Sound diary: caregivers log a sound, place, loudness, and the child's reaction in under 30 seconds, for 1–2 weeks.
The diary produces a pattern summary (most frequent sounds, places, sound types and reaction levels) with raw counts shown.
Countdown warnings ('blender in 3…2…1') are silent visual countdowns that the child can start, and use no sound of their own.
A full-screen 'too loud' signal card is available from Child Mode and Parent Mode.

The graded-exposure planner runs only after the caregiver confirms they are present. It uses small volume steps, a hard ceiling, at most one step up per session, a distress check-in at each step, and stop rules the child can trigger.
The toolkit prompts caregivers to arrange a hearing test with an audiologist and an OT sensory assessment, and never offers a diagnosis.
The toolkit shows sound-sensitivity strategies, including ear-defender guidance with the situational-use caution.
Caregivers pick 1–3 measurable goals from goal templates, each with a baseline and a target.
Daily goal logs take 30 seconds or less (a 0–4 scale per goal plus an optional note).
The app generates a review at 8–12 weeks that shows raw counts next to any summary, and the caregiver edits it before sharing.
The review exports as a plain-text or printable summary for the therapist, speech therapist or school. The caregiver chooses to share it.
Picture cards are used for song and instrument choice. Each card has a label, an icon and an accessible name, and no reading is required.
Choices work by touch alone. An optional spoken label plays only on a tap, through the safety chain.
The Education Hub gives plain-language summaries of each evidence tier and each intervention type.
The 'Is this therapy proven?' red-flag checker walks the caregiver through a claim checklist and returns an evidence-based verdict.
The hub explains why AIT, Tomatis, SSP, Samonas and similar programmes, frequency music and sound baths are unverified. The app offers none of them as a feature.
The disclaimer (D-001) appears during onboarding, in the hub, and in every exported review.
The five-question checklist for choosing a music therapist, with links to national credentialing bodies and no paid rankings.
A web portal lets therapists (with MFA and verified credentials) assign activities and view the logs a caregiver has shared.
Caregiver wellbeing: short encouragement, respite reminders and support-group links. No mental-health assessment.
Child Mode enforces a hard output ceiling on master gain and a peak limiter. No code path can exceed the ceiling.
No audio starts without a user tap. There is no autoplay at start-up or when a screen opens.
All audio fades in (at least 500 ms in Child Mode, 250 ms in Parent Mode).
Every child-facing screen shows a permanent Stop / Too Loud control. It silences all audio within 200 ms.
Graded-exposure limits: step at most +3 dB, at most one step up per session, a ceiling at least 6 dB below the Child Mode ceiling, and a start at -40 dBFS or quieter.

Stop rules: a child 'too loud' press or a caregiver distress rating of 3 or more stops the exposure at once, and the next session starts two steps lower. Two stops in a row lock the plan for 24 hours and advise contacting an OT or audiologist.
The session volume cannot rise sharply: at most +6 dB per second when the user changes it, never an instant jump.
Leaving Child Mode needs a parental gate (press and hold plus an adult challenge). The Back and Escape keys and tab switching do not leave Child Mode.
The safety core runs offline and does not rely on the network or any AI component.
The app shows a headphone safety notice and a reminder to keep device volume moderate the first time Child Mode is used.
Before any child data is stored, a caregiver gives consent through an adult gate plus an explicit consent screen. Consent is recorded with a version and a timestamp.
All data stays on the device in the MVP. There are no ads, no third-party trackers or analytics SDKs, and no network calls except an optional, opt-in coach call.
Data minimisation: the child is stored as a nickname and an age band only, with no birth date, photo or diagnosis.
Retention: logs older than the retention window (365 days by default; sound diary 90 days) are deleted automatically. 'Delete all data' wipes everything at once.
Withdrawing consent stops all data collection and offers deletion.
Role-based permissions (caregiver, child, therapist, allied professional, admin) are enforced by the deterministic core. Allied professionals are read-only by default.
The audit log is append-only, hash-chained and holds no personal data.
The data export gives the caregiver a machine-readable copy of all stored data.
The Activity Recommender recommends only activities from the curated library and explains each choice.
The Caregiver Coach answers only from approved knowledge passages and cites the passage IDs. If no passage supports an answer, it says it does not know.
The coach refuses questions about diagnosis, medication, dosage and cures with approved templates, and points to a clinician.
The coach detects distress, crisis and safeguarding signals and escalates to human help (emergency services, crisis lines) before anything else.
The coach states that it is an AI and resists prompt injection. Text from users or passages can never change its rules.
The Progress Summariser never overstates results. It shows the raw counts, contains no banned claims, and its output is editable before sharing.
The Content Compliance Checker blocks publication of any content item with a banned claim, a missing source, tier or reviewer, or an out-of-date review.
The coach works fully offline in grounded-extractive mode. The optional LLM mode is opt-in, and its output must pass the same deterministic post-checks or it is replaced.
Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 AA, 48 dp or larger touch targets, screen-reader labels, and a dyslexia-friendly font option.
Sensory-friendly visuals: no flashing or strobing, reduced motion by default, and a muted palette.
Everything works offline except sync and LLM chat. The app shell is cached by a service worker.
All user-facing strings are externalised, so they can be localised.
Content governance: every activity has a version, source citation, evidence tier, reviewer and review date.
Performance: the interactive drum responds in under 50 ms of scheduling latency, and the app shell becomes interactive quickly on a mid-range device.
